brent.why3m: driven by the 2026 Iran war: the Strait of Hormuz closure (from 28 Feb 2026) sent Brent up over 55% at its peak, reaching 142.2 (index) in April 2026. A US-Iran ceasefire memorandum (17 June 2026) triggered a partial retracement, but the index remains well above its pre-war level — trading desks widely cite a return to pre-war levels only by end of Q3 2026 at the earliest.
brent.why24m: steady post-2022 energy-crisis normalisation through 2023-2025 was interrupted by the 2026 Iran war shock — the sharpest, most disruptive single event in this library's 42-month window for any crude-linked series.

ethylene-propylene-na.why3m: tracks Brent/naphtha cracker feedstock economics directly — the same 2026 Iran war shock that hit crude fed straight through to olefins costs with only a short lag.
ethylene-propylene-na.why24m: a multi-year decline through 2024-25 (new olefins capacity in Asia/Middle East outpacing demand growth, compressing cracker margins) was sharply reversed by the 2026 war shock, a genuine trend break rather than a continuation of the prior oversupply story.

methanol-na.why3m: the single most dramatic war-driven move of any commodity in this library — Methanex's own posted NA price roughly tripled from ~$850/MT (Jan 2026) to $1,480/MT (Apr-May 2026), a +74% swing, reflecting methanol's double exposure: natural gas feedstock cost plus Middle East production/logistics disruption (Iran supplies ~5% of global methanol).
methanol-na.why24m: a normal gas-price-following decline through 2023-2025 (from 2022 energy-crisis highs to a ~$600-620/MT floor) was overwhelmed by the 2026 war shock in a single quarter — the steepest quarter-over-quarter move in the whole dataset.

dap.why3m: NOT meaningfully exposed to the Iran war — DAP supply routes (US Gulf, Morocco, Russia, China) mostly bypass the Strait of Hormuz. The Q3 2025 spike to $771/mt reflected North African (Morocco/Algeria) phosphate rock supply tightness and rising ammonia cost pass-through, and had already partially reversed by Q1 2026.
dap.why24m: driven by structural phosphate-rock supply tightness and ammonia-cost pass-through, not the 2026 war — one of the few commodities in this library whose 2026 movement is genuinely decoupled from the Hormuz shock.

cpo.why3m: NOT war-related — palm oil supply routes are entirely unaffected by the Strait of Hormuz. Near a 42-month low on persistent Indonesian/Malaysian production growth outpacing biodiesel absorption; EUDR (EU Deforestation Regulation) compliance cost is the other live driver, not yet fully reflected in price.
cpo.why24m: a structural oversupply story: palm oil production expansion from 2016-2020 plantings is now flowing through as sustained output growth, a multi-year bearish trend with no relation to any 2026 geopolitical event.

pko.why3m: moves with CPO as a co-product of palm oil milling (r=0.91 correlation) — same Indonesian/Malaysian oversupply story, not war-related.
pko.why24m: same structural palm-oil oversupply arc as CPO; the PKO/CPO spread reflects relative demand for C12-C14 vs C16-C18 oleochemical chains, not a geopolitical story.

corn.why3m: NOT exposed to the Iran war — US/Brazil/Argentina/Ukraine corn supply routes bypass Hormuz entirely. Near 42-month lows as the 2022 Ukraine-war supply premium has fully unwound.
corn.why24m: the 2022 Ukraine-war price spike fully reversed through 2023-2024 on record global harvests, followed by a partial 2025-26 recovery — a completely separate geopolitical story from the 2026 Iran war affecting most other commodities in this library.

elec-cn.why3m: NDRC-regulated tariff — a policy decision, not a market price, and structurally insulated from the Iran war's effect on global gas/oil markets. Essentially flat.
elec-cn.why24m: a modest multi-year decline via periodic NDRC tariff adjustments as Chinese renewable capacity additions continue at record pace, though the gap between regulated tariffs and actual generation cost is widening.

iron-scrap-na.why3m: choppy but range-bound — US EAF steel mill utilisation has stayed near its long-run average with no acute scrap shortage signal; a renewed early-2026 uptick is not yet confirmed as a sustained trend.
iron-scrap-na.why24m: driven by short scrap-collection cycles and steel mill restocking rather than any single structural event — the most range-bound base-chemicals-adjacent series in this library, tracking construction-demolition activity more than geopolitics.

elec-eu.why3m: continuing a genuine structural decline as TTF gas normalises and EU renewable capacity (47% of generation in 2024) keeps expanding — notably NOT showing the same war premium seen in gas-linked series, since renewables are increasingly setting the marginal price instead of gas.
elec-eu.why24m: the 2022 energy-crisis premium (index briefly near 118) has fully unwound; renewables overtaking gas as the EU's price-setting technology in a growing share of hours is a genuine structural bearish driver independent of any single event.

sulfuric-acid-na.why3m: a genuine, well-documented 2026 supply shock: the Iran war disrupted Persian Gulf sulfuric acid exports, and China separately halted its own exports to protect domestic supply — a double supply-side squeeze on a market that's structurally a smelter byproduct, not a purpose-made chemical.
sulfuric-acid-na.why24m: roughly doubled off its 2023-24 trough as smelter byproduct supply tightened relative to fertiliser/water-treatment/metals-processing demand — a sustained, multi-year tightening trend, not just a 2026 spike.

aluminum.why3m: a layered story: energy-transition demand (EV/solar/grid buildout) had already been driving a multi-year uptrend before the 2026 war added a further smelting-energy cost premium on top — unlike pure crude/gas plays, this one has a genuine structural demand component that won't fully unwind even if the war premium does.
aluminum.why24m: sustained appreciation since 2023 driven primarily by energy-transition demand growth, with the 2026 war adding an incremental (not primary) premium via smelting electricity costs — one of the few metals in this library where the structural story predates and outlasts the 2026 shock.

benzene-na.why3m: a bundled US aromatics PPI (benzene+toluene+xylene, not benzene alone) — the recent jump is consistent with the broader 2026 Iran war naphtha/crude shock, though the specific magnitude should be treated with caution given the bundling.
benzene-na.why24m: historically one of the most volatile series in this library (this proxy has ranged from ~88 to 480+ across its full history) reflecting exposure to both crude swings and refinery-margin/turnaround cycles simultaneously.

elec-na.why3m: minimal war exposure — cheap US shale gas continues to anchor domestic electricity costs structurally below global benchmarks.
elec-na.why24m: has tracked Henry Hub gas closely; US shale gas abundance keeps this the most consistently low-cost major electricity series in this library.

fatty-acids-ppi.why3m: tracks oleochemical/vegetable-oil feedstock cycles rather than the crude/gas complex directly — movement here reflects palm/tallow/soy supply dynamics more than the Iran war specifically.
fatty-acids-ppi.why24m: follows the broader vegetable-oil and animal-fat commodity cycle, distinct from the energy-driven story dominating most other series in this library over the same window.

refinery-gases-ppi.why3m: the same naphtha/NGL cracker-feedstock story as ethylene/propylene — moves with the 2026 Iran war oil shock via the shared feedstock relationship.
refinery-gases-ppi.why24m: steady decline through 2024-25 (new olefins capacity outpacing demand) reversed sharply by the 2026 war — mirrors the ethylene/propylene arc exactly, since it's built from the same underlying BLS series family.

urea.why3m: a genuine, severe 2026 supply shock: Iran (the world's 4th-largest urea exporter) was effectively removed from export markets, and Gulf logistics disruption from the Hormuz closure compounded the effect — prices nearly doubled from ~$385-415/mt pre-war to $726/mt in March 2026, with Northern Hemisphere spring planting-season demand adding further pressure on top.
urea.why24m: fell sharply through 2023 as the 2022 gas-crisis premium unwound, recovered gradually through 2024-25 on tightening Middle East supply even before the war, then spiked acutely in the 2026 disruption — a genuine compounding of a pre-existing tightening trend with a severe new shock.

ttf-eu.why3m: the EU gas benchmark spiked on the 2026 Iran war's effect on global LNG/gas flows and hasn't meaningfully retraced as of the latest data — European buyers remain exposed to elevated feedstock costs for any gas-linked chemical.
ttf-eu.why24m: the 2022 energy-crisis premium had substantially unwound by 2024-25 before the 2026 war reintroduced a new, still-unresolved price shock.

silicon-metal-mb.why3m: tracks a China-driven power-curtailment and oversupply cycle rather than the Iran war specifically — silicon smelting is extremely energy-intensive and historically prone to sharp swings tied to Chinese hydro/dry-season electricity availability.
silicon-metal-mb.why24m: a genuine boom-bust cycle: a 2024 price spike (well-documented China power-curtailment pattern) crashed to a multi-year low by mid-2025 on oversupply, with only a partial 2026 recovery — a fundamentally different driver from the crude/gas-linked series dominating this library.

gas-china.why3m: genuinely moving in the OPPOSITE direction from the global 2026 gas shock — China's NDRC-regulated industrial gas tariffs have continued easing even as TTF/JKM spiked, reflecting policy-driven price insulation rather than market exposure to the Hormuz disruption.
gas-china.why24m: a policy-driven, gradually softening trend, structurally decoupled from the global gas-price story dominating this library's other gas-linked series over the same window.

natgas-na.why3m: minimal war exposure — US shale gas abundance has kept Henry Hub structurally cheap and largely insulated from the Hormuz-driven LNG/TTF spike affecting Europe and Asia.
natgas-na.why24m: has stayed in a low, stable range for most of the window, the calmest major energy series in this library — a genuine structural advantage of US domestic shale supply.

lime-na.why3m: a low-value, high-volume mineral where freight cost to the nearest kiln typically dominates delivered price more than any single event — no acute 2026 disruption specific to lime itself.
lime-na.why24m: USGS data shows China alone accounts for ~72% of global lime output; pricing here reflects regional plant proximity and freight economics more than any geopolitical driver.

ammonia-na.why3m: a bundled US nitrogen-products PPI (ammonia+nitric acid+ammonium compounds+urea) — shows a real but comparatively muted war-linked uptick versus global benchmarks, since the US benefits from cheap domestic shale gas versus Europe/Asia's greater reliance on Middle East-linked gas and LNG.
ammonia-na.why24m: a steep 2023 decline (2022 gas-crisis unwind) followed by gradual 2024-25 recovery, then a sharp early-2026 acceleration tied to the broader gas-market disruption — cross-check against Henry Hub before assuming this specific bundle reflects pure ammonia dynamics.

zinc.why3m: essentially flat — no structural demand catalyst (unlike copper/aluminum's energy-transition story) and no acute 2026 supply disruption specific to zinc.
zinc.why24m: the most range-bound major metal in this library over the full window — a genuine round trip back near its Jan 2023 starting level, reflecting a market in approximate supply/demand balance.

elec-in.why3m: rising modestly on domestic industrial demand growth and capacity constraints, largely independent of the 2026 war — India's own growth trajectory is the dominant driver, not Middle East gas exposure.
elec-in.why24m: a steady upward trend as industrial electricity demand growth outpaces capacity additions — a genuinely different driver from the war-linked volatility affecting Europe/Asia gas-linked electricity.

caustic-soda-na.why3m: near a structural multi-year low — persistent Asian (particularly Chinese) chlor-alkali capacity additions have kept this oversupplied even as other chemicals spiked on the 2026 war.
caustic-soda-na.why24m: one of the largest sustained declines of any index in this library (~30% off its Jan 2023 level) — new capacity growth in Asia has structurally outpaced demand for several years running, a trend the 2026 war has not reversed.

silicon-metal-cn.why3m: same China power-curtailment/oversupply story as the broader silicon metal complex — not war-linked.
silicon-metal-cn.why24m: tracks the same 2024-spike-then-2025-crash cycle documented for silicon metal generally, driven by Chinese energy availability and smelting capacity utilisation.
